**State: RUNNING** — every figure below re-measured by the controller against

## The finding

**189,483 of namespace `rico`'s raw turns are captured, stored, and never
distilled — because no `memory.distill` job has EVER been enqueued for that
namespace.** The distiller is not broken. It has never been pointed at the
namespace holding 98.5% of the corpus.

```
select namespace, state, count(*) from maintenance_jobs
where job_kind='memory.distill' group by 1,2;

 geetesh | succeeded | 177
 lisa    | succeeded | 147
 kevin   | succeeded |  64
 admin   | succeeded |   3
                        ---
                        391   <- zero rows for 'rico'

select count(*) from maintenance_jobs
where namespace='rico' and job_kind='memory.distill';  ->  0
```

Every namespace that IS enqueued distills at 100%. `rico` is at 2.58%:

```
select namespace, count(*) total, count(distilled_at) distilled,
       round(100.0*count(distilled_at)/count(*),2) pct
from ob_raw_turns group by 1 order by 2 desc;

 rico    | 194511 | 5028 |   2.58
 lisa    |   2377 | 2377 | 100.00
 geetesh |    250 |  250 | 100.00
 kevin   |    176 |  176 | 100.00
 admin   |      9 |    9 | 100.00
```

Undistilled backlog for `rico`: **189,483 turns.**

## The cliff: 2026-07-29

The 5,028 `rico` turns that ARE distilled came from a pre-queue path that
stopped dead:

```
select created_at::date, count(*), count(distilled_at) from ob_raw_turns
where namespace='rico' and created_at between '2026-07-26' and '2026-08-01'
group by 1 order by 1;

 2026-07-26 | 10177 | 1606
 2026-07-27 |  9290 | 1903
 2026-07-28 |  6572 |  128
 2026-07-29 |  3921 |    0   <- and 0 every day since
 2026-07-30 |  5464 |    0
 2026-07-31 |  3580 |    0
```

The queue-based distiller first ran **2026-08-08** (`min(created_at)` over
`memory.distill` jobs) and has run 391 jobs through 2026-08-24 — none for
`rico`. So there is a **ten-day gap with no distiller at all**, followed by a
distiller that runs daily for four other namespaces and skips this one.

## Why this looked like "capture collapsed" and was not

`ob_session_events` shows 2026-06: 2912, 2026-07: 7673, 2026-08: 1062, which
reads as capture dying. Both halves of that reading are wrong:

1. **July was inflated, not August depressed.** 5,080 of July's 7,673 events
   (66%) landed in 2026-07-13..18 from `codex-session-finalization` /
   `claude-session-finalization`, and their CONTENT is May/June session logs —
   a one-time historical import written on one date. 2026-07-13 alone is 3,742
   events, 49% of the month. Organic July is ~2,593 against August's ~1,063
   over 25 days.

2. **Raw capture ROSE 4x and is healthy.** `ob_raw_turns` went 40,805 (July,
   and the table only exists from 07-25, so that is 7 days) to 156,678
   (August), newest row 2026-08-25. August days routinely run 7,000-13,719
   turns. What fell is the DISTILLED layer, which isolates the fault to the
   distillation stage.

The volume also migrated tables: `source='shared'` was writing prompts
directly into `ob_session_events` and falls 220/day on 07-31 to 25 on 08-01 to
effectively 0 after 08-04, exactly as `ob_raw_turns` scales up.

## Why this is the one that matters

This is the mechanism behind "no agent can recall anything." It stacks with
two already-filed defects, and all three must be fixed for recall to work:

- **#744 D1** — a bare `recall` never asks for durable memory at all
  (asymmetric section default, `server/tools/agent-context-pack.ts:139`).
- **#433 defect 1** — `ob_session_events` is absent from `ALL_TABLES`, so even
  an explicit durable request cannot reach session events.
- **#433 defect 2** — nothing promotes lane events into `thoughts`/`decisions`;
  those tables are frozen at 2026-08-08, 17 days stale.
- **THIS ISSUE** — and even if all three above were fixed, `ob_session_events`
  would still be missing essentially all of August's real material, because
  189,483 turns were never distilled into it.

Fixing recall without this leaves recall correctly searching an empty shelf.

## Ask

1. Enqueue `memory.distill` for namespace `rico` — the immediate unblock.
2. Backfill the 189,483-turn backlog (operator call: this is a large embed/LLM
   spend and should be scoped and scheduled, not run blind from a lane).
3. Name why the namespace was never enqueued — a hardcoded list, a config
   default, or an onboarding step nobody ran. Until that is known, the same
   gap can reappear for the next namespace.
4. Add a done-means assertion that FAILS when any namespace with raw turns has
   zero distill jobs. This was invisible for 27 days precisely because nothing
   asserted it; every job that ran reported `succeeded`.

Not proposing the fix here — filing the measurement.

### rodaddy — 2026-08-25T05:55:47Z

## ROOT CAUSE FOUND — RUNNING, reproduced outside the service

My original framing in this issue ("no job was ever enqueued for `rico`") was
the symptom, not the cause, and the "namespace" reading was wrong. There is no
namespace allowlist anywhere in the producer. **The selection query cannot
select this namespace's work at all, and the mechanism is a ranking window that
ranks the wrong set.**

### The mechanism

`selectDistillLaneBatches` (`src/maintenance-sweep.ts:59-135`) builds
`window_turns` from EVERY turn in a selected session — it filters only on
`retention_tier = 'live'` and carries `distilled_at IS NULL` along as a boolean
column, `is_due`:

```sql
window_turns AS (
  SELECT t.id, ..., (t.distilled_at IS NULL) AS is_due
    FROM ob_raw_turns t
    JOIN ranked_sessions s ON ...
   WHERE t.retention_tier = 'live'          -- <-- no distilled_at predicate
),
ranked_window_turns AS (
  SELECT *, row_number() OVER (
           PARTITION BY lane_id, namespace
           ORDER BY session_ref NULLS LAST, occurred_at NULLS LAST, id
         ) AS turn_rank
    FROM window_turns                        -- <-- ranks DONE turns too
)
```

`due_lanes` then counts `FILTER (WHERE w.is_due AND w.turn_rank <= $2)`.

So already-distilled turns occupy rank positions, and `turn_rank` is compared
against the batch bound. Measured on the live dogfood DB as the SERVICE ROLE:

```
due_in_window : 5921     -- undistilled turns inside the window
processable   : 0        -- how many qualify
min_due_rank  : 1501     -- rank of the FIRST due turn
max_rank      : 7991
```

The first genuinely-due turn ranks **1501st**, one position past the bound of
1500. Ranks 1-1500 are turns that were already distilled back in July. They are
re-ranked on every tick, consume the whole window every time, and the due work
is never reachable.

Counting the window directly:

```
already_done_in_window : 2070
due_in_window          : 5921
processable            : 0
```

### Proof of the fix direction

Same query, same params, with the window ranking only due turns
(`... FROM window_turns WHERE is_due`):

```
processable : 1500
```

Zero to a full batch, from moving one predicate. No bound was changed.

### Why every signal stayed green

This is the failure mode worth naming. Nothing was broken enough to alarm:

- `/health` reports `maintenance_producer: {stale: false, completed_ticks: 1156}`
  and `capture: {reason: "capture lane delivering"}` — status `healthy`.
- `maintenance_sweep_complete` logs every 5s with
  `distill_batches_selected: 0, distill_batches_deferred: 0,
   distill_turns_deferred: 0`.
- **Zero deferrals is the tell.** If the sweep were seeing the backlog and
  taking a slice, the remainder would be reported deferred and the bound
  warning would fire. It reports nothing deferred because the query genuinely
  finds nothing processable — so the one signal that would have exposed a
  189,662-turn backlog reads identical to "all caught up."
- `scripts/done-means/625-sweep-heartbeat.sh` PASSES 5/5. It gates producer
  LIVENESS (does a tick complete?), not producer YIELD (does a tick that
  completes ever select anything?). The producer is perfectly alive and
  perfectly idle, and 625 is satisfied by that.
- 123 nonzero ticks out of 51,614 in the log window, every one `selected 1,
  enqueued 1` — the trickle from sessions small enough to fit under rank 1500.
  That trickle is why `maintenance_jobs` is not empty and why the distiller
  itself looks fine: `distill_sweep_complete` shows `units: 6, turns_stamped: 6,
  candidates_written: 6, succeeded`. The distiller works. It is starved.

### Corrections to this issue's earlier claims

- WRONG: "no `memory.distill` job has ever been enqueued for namespace `rico`."
  RIGHT: jobs ARE enqueued for `rico` (that is what the 123 ticks did), just
  vanishingly few. The `maintenance_jobs` grouping I read showed four other
  namespaces because `rico`'s handful had already aged out of the retained rows.
- WRONG: implying the other namespaces are configured differently. RIGHT: they
  distill at 100% because they are TINY (lisa 2377, geetesh 250, kevin 176,
  admin 9). Every one of their sessions fits under rank 1500. `rico` has 194,594
  turns, so it is the only namespace large enough to expose the defect. Nothing
  is namespace-specific; the bug is size-specific.
- `lane_id IS NULL` on every namespace including the ones that work, so the null
  lane is not implicated. `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` handles it by design.

### Verified environment

Reproduced with a standalone script running `runMaintenanceSweep` against the
service's own env (`/Volumes/ThunderBolt/open-brain-local/local-clone.env`),
connected as `open_brain_local_clone` to `open_brain_local_20260724` —
`selected: 0`, matching the live service exactly. Not a permissions artifact:
the service role sees all 189,662 rows, and `ob_raw_turns` has no RLS
(`relrowsecurity = f`, zero policies).

### Ask

1. Add the `distilled_at IS NULL` predicate to `window_turns` so the ranking
   window ranks only work that needs doing. Operator has authorized backfilling
   ALL of it, so no bound changes are in scope here.
2. RED-first done-means: a gate that FAILS when a namespace has undistilled
   turns and the sweep reports zero processable. #625 covers liveness; nothing
   covers yield, which is why this ran 27 days invisibly.
3. The serving tree (`/Volumes/ThunderBolt/open-brain-local/app`, revision

   copy of the query — the fix has to reach it, not just `main`.

### rodaddy — 2026-08-25T07:01:24Z

## Second defect found and fixed: the CLAIM discarded the due turns

`36a0b6e` on `fix/recall-serves-durable-memory`. RUNNING on the local dogfood
service (`/health` reports `revision: 36a0b6e`, pid 3273).

The producer fix (`2a0eab1`) was necessary and not sufficient. With it in
place the sweep enqueued jobs correctly and *still* stamped nothing, because
the consumer declined to claim the work the producer had queued.

### What `claimDistillBatch` did

`src/distill-window.ts` selected each due session WHOLE and then applied
`LIMIT maxTurns` to the combined result. Reading whole sessions is correct and
deliberate: an already-distilled turn reappearing in a claim is the context
that makes a short current turn interpretable, which is the premise of the
module. Applying the bound *afterwards* was the defect. Ordered by
`session_ref, occurred_at, id`, a long-running session's already-distilled
history filled every one of the 1500 slots and the due turns fell off the end.

Measured against the live corpus, namespace `rico`, production parameters
(`maxSessions=4`, `maxTurns=1500`):

| | due in claim | context in claim | backlog |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 0 | 1500 | 190,102 |
| after | 980 | 551 | 190,118 |

A claim of 1500 turns containing nothing to do.

### Why it reported success

`runDistillSweep` stamps only `if (consumedTurnIds.length > 0)`
(`src/distill-handler.ts`). An empty claim stamped nothing, threw nothing, and
returned — so the job completed as `succeeded`.

It then wedged the producer. The idempotency key is
`` `${batchHash}:s${maxSessions}:t${maxTurns}` `` over the DUE turns, inserted
`ON CONFLICT (job_kind, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING`
(`src/maintenance-queue.ts:370`). The code states the assumption directly:
*"consuming any due turn changes the watermark, so a succeeded job cannot
block the lane's next window."* True only if something consumes. Nothing did,
so the hash never changed and every later enqueue was silently dropped, while
the sweep kept logging `distill_jobs_enqueued: 1` on every tick.

Observed: **392 succeeded `memory.distill` jobs, zero turns stamped since
2026-08-24, no error anywhere.** Newest job row 02:19, four hours before a
deploy whose own logs claimed an enqueue every 5s.

This is the same family as the producer defect one layer down — the bound
applied to the wrong set. Fixing either alone yields nothing.

### The fix

`due_turns` takes `maxTurns`; `context_turns` is derived from whichever due
turns survive it, expressed as a `session_seq` range joined per `session_ref`
so a claim can never pull an unrelated session's tail. Context is governed by
`contextWindow` per due turn rather than counted against `maxTurns` — that
bound governs the WORK, and conflating it with the reading around the work is
what broke this.

### Empty claims are no longer silent

A drained queue and a broken claim were indistinguishable and both returned
without a word, which is what let this run 27 days unseen. The terminal path
now counts outstanding due turns and emits `distill_claim_empty_with_backlog`
with the number when work remains, `distill_queue_drained` when it does not.
Deliberately not an error: the sweep did not fail, and throwing would fail a
job whose own behaviour was correct.

### Receipts

- Gate `scripts/done-means/747-distill-claim-yields.sh`, written RED against
  the live corpus (`due in claim: 0`), now PASS (`980 due / 551 context`).
- Gate `747-distill-sweep-yields.sh` (producer) still PASS.
- Gate `685-live-roles-not-accept-roles.sh` still PASS.
- `bun run test:isolated src/distill-window.test.ts src/distiller.test.ts
  src/distill-exchange.test.ts` -> 121 pass, 0 fail, including two new
  regression tests covering bound placement and the session-scoped context
  range.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Not covered

Whether the 190,149-turn backlog actually drains end to end is being measured
now and is NOT yet claimed. Recall (#744), session-event visibility (#433),
and the client contract (#742) are untouched by this commit.

### rodaddy — 2026-08-25T12:06:21Z

## The lane was DEADLOCKED, and it is now draining

`acca7d7` on `fix/recall-serves-durable-memory`. RUNNING on the local dogfood
service (`/health` reports `revision: acca7d7`).

**Result: `distilled` 8,028 -> 9,528 (+1,500, one full batch), `due` 190,206 ->
188,707, a second job `running`.** First forward progress since 2026-07-29.

Three more defects sat behind the claim fix (36a0b6e). Each one alone was
enough to stop the pipeline, and each was invisible.

### 1. A dropped insert was counted as an enqueued job (`a61b99d`)

`MaintenanceQueue.enqueue` inserts `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and, when the
insert is dropped, returns the row that already held the key. It returns a
`MaintenanceJob` either way. The sweep did `jobs.push(await enqueue(...))`
unconditionally and reported `jobs.length`, so it could not tell a job it had
just created from one that succeeded six hours earlier.

That is why the log read `distill_jobs_enqueued: 1` every 5 seconds while the
newest row in `maintenance_jobs` stayed six hours old. Both statements were
true.

`enqueue` now reports `enqueueOutcome: "created" | "deduped"`; the sweep counts
only created jobs and surfaces `distill_jobs_deduped`. Immediately after
deploy the log read:

```
distill_jobs_enqueued: 0, distill_jobs_deduped: 1
```

The condition that was invisible for 27 days became one line.

### 2. A succeeded job reserved its idempotency key forever (`acca7d7`, 047)

026 declared `UNIQUE (job_kind, idempotency_key)` across every state, and
nothing in this repo deletes from `maintenance_jobs` -- there is no reaper. So
a `succeeded` job held its key permanently.

```
blocking row : 9c29069d-267c-4e39-a135-ace207e342f6
state        : succeeded, 02:19:05, attempts 1
key          : memory.distill:25ab14fc...:s4:t1500
live hash    : 25ab14fc...   (byte-identical, verified against the corpus)
```

The hash cannot drift on its own: it covers the first 1500 due turns in
`(session_ref, occurred_at, id)` order, and new turns sort to the END where
they never enter that window. The lane could not self-heal at any backlog
size, and every insert for hours was dropped against a job that had stamped
nothing.

Migration 047 scopes uniqueness to live jobs (`state IN ('queued','running')`)
via a partial unique index. A queued or running job still reserves its key, so
concurrent producers cannot double-enqueue and the at-least-once queue stays
idempotent. A terminal job releases it.

This does NOT make redoing finished work automatic. A key only recurs when a
producer recomputes it from live state, which for distill means the turns are
still due. The guard against redoing completed work is the producer's
`distilled_at IS NULL` predicate; leaning on a permanently-held row instead is
what turned one unconsumed batch into a permanent deadlock.

Class fix -- the deadlock was available to any job kind whose key recurs.

Verified post-deploy: two rows now share that key, which the blanket
constraint made impossible, and the newer one (`4eeb1689`, 08:05:02) is the
first new distill job since 02:19.

### 3. Swallowed errors, per STANDARDS-observability.md

Operator flagged this class. Audited all 246 TypeScript files in `src/` and
`server/` with brace-matched scanning: **62 catch sites with no log and no
re-raise.** Many report through a helper (`reportSinkFailure`, `noteSkip`) and
are compliant; the count is the audit ceiling, not the violation count.

One was mine, introduced in 36a0b6e: the backlog probe caught and set `null`
silently. That would have recreated, inside the detector, the exact
silent-fallback defect the detector exists to catch. Now logs
`distill_backlog_probe_failed` and stays fail-open by documented decision.

The remaining sites are not this issue's scope; worth their own pass.

### Receipts

- `distilled` 8,028 -> 9,528 measured live, `due` 190,206 -> 188,707.
- Sweep log shows `distill_jobs_enqueued: 0, distill_jobs_deduped: 1` on the
  wedged state, before 047 cleared it.
- `bun run test:isolated` on `maintenance-queue`, `maintenance-queue.pg`,
  `maintenance-sweep` -> 33 pass, 0 fail.
- The dedupe regression test proven RED against the old counting behaviour
  before being accepted as passing.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; migration 047 applied.

### Not covered

Whether the full 188,707-turn backlog drains to zero is being measured now.
Recall (#744), session-event visibility (#433), and the client contract (#742)
are untouched.
